description: Plan step R2 (graph node rules). Extend the rules board's storage from the thin slice (peakMode only) to the full state shape and the full repository file, including the repo-file adoption/restore handling. Crash safety and audit: deep review. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Read rules design sec 7.1-7.5 completely (files, ProjectState shape, write order, read/recovery, repo file comparison table at the end of 7.5), sec 14 and sec 15 R2 (including the 0.9 additions). Read the existing src/rules/store.ts, repo.ts, model.ts, tests/rules-store.spec.ts and the slice's orchestrator ruling in design-context.md ('Rules thin slice'): a collection that is empty is absent from the stored state and from every digest, so every digest the slice wrote stays valid.

Write specs first (extend tests/rules-store.spec.ts, real temp dirs, real git repos via git init): a state/journal/rules.json written by the slice code (only peakMode) replays byte-for-byte with unchanged digests under the new model; empty new collections never appear in a snapshot, record digest or rules.json; every row of the end-of-7.5 comparison table (fresh clone starts from the file and writes a base record; file changed outside the engine -> not in effect, one repo-outside record per digest, .rules.json.outside-* copy, cleared when restored; git checkout of an old version; hand edit; .git/MERGE_HEAD present -> write goes to journal and snapshot only, repo-written.json untouched, written after the mark disappears; repo-adopt and repo-restore results); script references read from the repo file are stored without approvedAt and a rule using one is listed as unapproved (impl-plan Interpretations 2); session-scoped rules never enter rules.json; repoPart/repoJson determinism (shuffled keys give the same text, two-space indent, trailing newline).

Implement: ProjectState gains rules, signals (definitions + manual values), tickets, notices, scripts (pin records {file, sha256, lang, approvedAt?}), nextTicket, proposals is NOT added (blocked); Change paths extend to two-level ['rules', id], ['signals', name], ['tickets', id], ['notices', id], ['scripts', id]; stateProblem validates them; RepoRules/repoPart/repoJson/parseRepoRules/diffRepo/stateFromRepo generalise to the person-decided part (peakMode, rules, switches with their person-set values, detectors, script pins); repo-adopt and repo-restore write paths in repo.ts; row-health.ts reports repo-outside and unapproved scripts. Keep applyRecord the only state transition and keep it clock-free.
Do not read the project graph here. The F84 branch 'script runs when the graph shows a done decision with the shown-text mark' is out of scope (needs M3 step 6); do not add a stub seam for it.
Docs in the same commit: docs/ORCHESTRATION.md section 16 storage description and docs/DESIGN.md if it lists the files.
Commit once: 'feat(rules): store the full rules state and the repository file (rules)' with gate results.

RepoRules = version, rules (project scope only), detectors, signals without detected, peakMode, scripts as {file, sha256, lang}. New pure functions adoptRepo(state, file, digest), unapprovedScripts(state) (standing no-pin | not-approved | changed, sorted by id), compareCodePoints (now exported). RuleContext has a new optional `stored: true` mode used by stateProblem/parseRepoRules (see interpretation 4). stateFromRepo = adoptRepo on an empty state with seq 1.

- repo.ts: adoptRepoLocked(paths, read, io) and restoreRepoLocked(paths, read, io) (records repo-adopt / repo-restore, actor human, target rules.json). They take the ProjectRead returned by settleLocked and must run under the write lock the caller holds. Design points that were interpreted, not followed (flag to the reviewer / orchestrator):
1. detectors are stored (ProjectState.detectors, Change path [detectors,id], RepoRules.detectors, Detector type with structural check). FEAT step 3 lists the Change paths without detectors but the same step and impl-plan R2 put detectors in repoPart and design 7.2 has them. Storage shape only: no producer, no runtime (R6 stays blocked).
2. Script pins in rules.json have no approvedAt (design 7.2 RepoRules.scripts included it). approvedAt is a record of this machine; parseRepoRules refuses a file that carries it ("scripts.<id>.approvedAt is not a field") so a hand edit cannot forge an approval. State pins are {file, sha256, lang, approvedAt?}; the design field `question` is not stored (the graph-approval branch of F84 is blocked on M3 step 6; add it with that branch). adoptRepo keeps the approval of a pin whose file, sha256 and lang are unchanged and drops it otherwise.
3. repo-adopt of a deleted rules.json is refused (reason names the restore way out) instead of adopting "nothing decided". repo-restore on a project where nothing is decided removes the added rules.json (copy kept in .llm/rules/.rules.json.outside-*); during a git operation that removal is deferred and the file is found as outside again until the person asks again. Design is silent on both.
4. Stored rules are checked by validateRule in `stored` mode: ttl in the past is accepted, a condition naming a signal that is not defined is accepted (comparison still checked, value types unchecked), project limits (50 rules, 10 scripts) are not applied. Reason: a stored rule must survive a later signal-delete or expiry without making the snapshot "corrupt" and triggering endless recoveries. Consequence for later steps: any stricter change to validateRule must stay backward compatible in stored mode, or old snapshots become unreadable. FEAT-004 signal-delete need not refuse deleting a referenced signal.
5. Fresh start from a file now means "the file decides anything", not only a peak level; a file that parses but decides nothing is in-sync. The whole file must pass parseRepoRules (entry by entry) or the file is `unreadable` and not used.
6. Crash ordering: fresh start and repo-adopt note repo-written.json BEFORE appending the record that names the digest; repo-restore removes repo-written.json BEFORE its record (so a deferred or failed write is "owed", not "outside"). exportRepo still records repo-written after writing the file, as before (design-accepted window; a crash there is read as in-sync until the next outside edit, which would then look owed: unchanged from the slice, not fixed here).
7. diffRepo lists fields in code point order (peakMode was level,at,origin before; now at,level for a changed level+at). Lines come in rules.json key order: detectors, peakMode, rules, scripts, signals, ids sorted. One existing assertion in rules-store.spec.ts was updated for the field order.
8. Change.cause (prune/expire, design 7.2) is not added: FEAT-004 adds it with cleanup and expiry planning.
